correctness.rationale: The distance table of the crown graph yields exact difference profiles for same-side, matched cross-side, and adjacent cross-side vertex pairs. These profiles prove the one-omitted-pair lower bound, the side-balance criterion for size \(n-1\), the impossibility of that size for \(3\le n\le6\), and the complete size-\(n\) classification. A standalone exhaustive checker confirms the theorem for every subset below and at the optimum through \(n=9\); this finite check is supporting evidence, not the infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The foundational paper gives general bounds and examples but no crown or complete-bipartite-minus-matching theorem. The closest matching-deletion theorem is for cocktail-party graphs \(K_{2m}-M\), a nonbipartite diameter-two family, so it does not dominate the diameter-three crown result.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Ordinary resolving sets are weaker than doubly resolving sets, so the crown metric-dimension result does not imply this claim. Cocktail-party graphs have a different adjacency and distance structure. The Kneser result concerns ordinary Kneser graphs. The foundational general bound \(\psi(G)\le |V(G)|-1\) gives only \(2n-1\) for the crown and is far weaker than the retained exact values.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Crown graph, complete bipartite graph minus a perfect matching, and bipartite Kneser terminology were all checked. The crown-specific metric-dimension record concerns ordinary resolving sets; the later Kneser paper defines and treats ordinary Kneser graphs rather than the bipartite Kneser crown family.

originality.rationale: The retained statement combines an exact phase transition, a complete structural classification of all bases, and exact counts. Focused searches and inspections found neighboring results for general doubly resolving sets, cocktail-party graphs, ordinary crown metric dimension, and ordinary Kneser graphs, but no source whose statement implies the crown theorem.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible paper may use an uncommon synonym for either crown graphs or doubly resolving sets.

The crown-specific 2018 article was available here as an abstract/database record rather than inspected full text; its abstract explicitly scopes ordinary metric dimension, so it was not used as a whole-document noncoverage certificate.

value.rationale: Crown graphs are a canonical symmetric matching-deleted bipartite family. The theorem exposes a nontrivial transition at \(n=7\), classifies every optimum set, and counts all bases. This is structurally stronger than a scalar value and is naturally relevant because the foundational theory links doubly resolving sets to metric dimension of Cartesian products.
